theater: US Army — XVIII Airborne Corps proving set
disclosure: A proving set, not a conflict picture. Every record rests on official US Army public-affairs pages or dated press reporting, chosen because resolution is unambiguous and nothing here is sensitive. Its purpose is to put the decay model under forecast: if a sixty-day half-life on command is calibrated, command-change projections issued at sixty days should resolve near fifty percent. Coordinates are installation centroids, approximate, and denote home station rather than any deployed position. Observation dates follow the Spion rule, observed at rather than checked at: where a source page carries no publication date, as_of is the date the page was retrieved.

existence.note: Official US Army unit page. Page carries no publication date, so as_of is the retrieval date.

location.note: Installation centroid, approximate. Home station, not a deployed position. A headquarters at its home station is the least interesting location claim there is and the easiest to keep fresh, which is exactly why it is the right place to start.

commander.name: Gregory K. Anderson
commander.note: In command since 2024-12-06. Last dated confirmation in post is the corps change-of-responsibility ceremony of 2026-06-15. SUCCESSION PENDING: Maj. Gen. John W. Lubas was nominated on 2026-07-17 for promotion to lieutenant general and assignment as commanding general of this corps, subject to Senate confirmation. The generated sixty-day baseline of fifty percent is knowably wrong on this record, which is the whole reason the baseline prints separately from a judgement.

formations.name: 82nd Airborne Division

existence.note: Official US Army unit page, undated, so as_of is the retrieval date.

composition.summary: Airborne infantry division specialising in joint forcible entry, described by the Army as the primary fighting arm of XVIII Airborne Corps, maintaining a rotating brigade-sized immediate response force.

location.note: Home station. Installation centroid, approximate. Read alongside the posture claim: elements were reported deploying elsewhere and that reporting has not been re-verified, so home station and posture sit in tension by design rather than by error.

posture.note: Between two and three thousand paratroopers, the majority of the division's immediate response force, were reported under written deployment orders to the Middle East, with the commanding general and headquarters staff also reported deploying. Single-source, attributed to an official not authorised to speak publicly. Not re-verified since. At roughly 125 days against a 21-day half-life this is the stalest claim in the file. It is retained rather than deleted because the age of the last observation is itself the finding.

commander.name: Brandon R. Tegtmeier
commander.note: Assumed command 2025-08-28 from Maj. Gen. James Work. Currently listed on the official division page, so as_of is the retrieval date.

formations.notes: The record that carries the whole argument: a fresh, well-sourced command claim sitting beside a four-month-old posture claim. Both are true as recorded. Only one of them is current.

formations.name: 3rd Infantry Division

existence.note: Entered on press reporting rather than an official unit page, and graded lower than the two Fort Bragg records on purpose, so the ladder is exercised by something real.

commander.name: John W. Lubas
commander.note: Nominated 2026-07-17 for promotion to lieutenant general and assignment as commanding general of XVIII Airborne Corps, subject to Senate confirmation. If confirmed, this claim and the XVIII Airborne Corps command claim flip on the same event, which makes any two projections issued against them correlated. Correlated rows are not independent observations against the thirty-resolution floor and must not be counted as two.

formations.notes: PARENT UNVERIFIED. This division's higher formation has not been checked against a source, so the field is left null rather than filled from memory. A visible gap is worth more than a plausible guess.
